The PRD v2 Success test that a restart keeps every booking must sign in again after the restart, since the same restart signs every user out (ADR-001 Consequences).

Carried from Q-015 (from S04), which matched S11 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a spec touch may not write the Phase Plan (DEC-103). Original text: ADR-002 for the integration plan: the browser tests run with the browser's time zone set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC (for example Asia/Kolkata, +05:30); the change-day tests take the next last Sunday of March and of October after the real clock, never a fixed date (2026-10-25 has passed; the next is 2027-03-28), and booking-api@v1's how-far-ahead limit decides whether that day is bookable through the API; the backend's clock decides 'started', which an end-to-end test cannot set, so the plan says which scripted test covers AC-5.5 and AC-6.2's started case (PRD v2 Success); the strings to assert are ADR-002 item 7's, including '23:00 to Fri 6 Nov 02:00' and '01:30 BST' / '01:30 GMT'.

Carried from Q-020 (from S05), which matched S11 by its node and was closed there as explained, unaddressed, because a spec touch may not write the Phase Plan (DEC-103). Original text: booking-api@v1 for the integration plan: the 365-day horizon keeps the next London clock-change day bookable through the API under the real clock (at most 217 days ahead from any moment, hsdd/auto/experiments/booking-api-fixtures/). PRD v2 Success's 20 simultaneous attempts must give exactly one 201 and nineteen 409 BOOKING_CONFLICT naming the winner (G5, G6); a restart keeps every booking and id but drops tokens, so the test signs in again (G17). The fixtures carry a fixed clock and seeded state that the real service under the real clock cannot reproduce: only the 14 that depend on neither (the eight 400s, the four 401s, cancel-unknown and cancel-malformed-id) can be replayed exactly through the proxy; the stateful criteria are this node's own tests. consumers names simple-login.integration.3 provisionally (DEC-053).

From S11's touch (DEC-099 to DEC-102). Owns now says the root package.json scripts run the real service with its PostgreSQL 17, started through simple-login.backend's Docker Compose service, beside the real web app; the database, the Compose service and its Compose file stay the backend's (DEC-081), and where the file lives is H14's choice (Q-031). Bookings now persist across runs of the suite, so a test that books a slot computed from the clock can meet an earlier run's booking (a second run's 20 simultaneous attempts would then all get 409); the plan decides how a test run gets a database of its own or clean slots, through the backend's Compose service or booking-api@v1; writing the backend's tables directly would tie this node to a schema simple-login.backend owns. The Overview leaves to this plan which scripted test covers a booking that has started (PRD v2 AC-5.5, AC-6.2; DEC-102): asking for a started time works through the API under the real clock, but a booking of one's own that has started appears only by waiting for its start.

Governed by stays [ADR-002] and ADR-001's affects does not name simple-login.integration. The Overview cites ADR-001 only beside auth-api@v1 G3 and booking-api@v1 G17, which carry its restart behaviour to this consumer; if the owner wants this node governed by ADR-001 directly, that is an hsdd-adr update, not a spec touch.

Routing mechanics, as in S09 and S10 (DEC-085, DEC-095): routed.mjs matches an item on a handoff to every step on that handoff's target, so the six H18 items reached this spec touch, and the carried copies will reach H13, the citation touch on the same node, before H18.
